clusters.pick_reason: 2692's close() groups outstanding request ids by their shared stream (correct for batched POSTs that map several request ids to one stream) and skips ids that already have a real response instead of clobbering them, then settles the rest with a JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' error — a response shape the MCP client already knows how to parse as a per-request error. 2600's changeset only describes answering with a blanket HTTP 404 'Session not found' for parked JSON-mode POSTs, which doesn't address batched request ids sharing one stream or preserve a response that already resolved. Note 2600 also independently clears `_requestToStreamMapping` in close() to fix a separate correlation-leak (stale request ids resolvable after close, causing send() to record undeliverable responses) — that portion is not covered by 2692's diff and should be re-applied on top of 2692 rather than dropped when 2600 is closed.

clusters.pick_reason: 2692's close() groups outstanding request ids by their shared stream (correct for batched POSTs that map several request ids to one stream) and skips ids that already have a real response instead of clobbering them, then settles the rest with a JSON-RPC -32000 'Connection closed' error — a response shape the MCP client already knows how to parse as a per-request error. 2600's changeset only describes answering with a blanket HTTP 404 'Session not found' for parked JSON-mode POSTs, which doesn't address batched request ids sharing one stream or preserve a response that already resolved. Note 2600 also independently clears `_requestToStreamMapping` in close() to fix a separate correlation-leak (stale request ids resolvable after close, causing send() to record undeliverable responses) — that portion is not covered by 2692's diff and should be re-applied on top of 2692 rather than dropped when 2600 is closed.
